surprise.title: The Hunter's Moon peaked just after midnight
surprise.body: October's full moon, traditionally called the Hunter's Moon, was exactly full at 12:12 AM this morning and is still 99% lit. Right now it is sinking in the west over a clear sky and sets at 8:17 AM, so a quick look out a west-facing window before work catches it. Tonight it rises at 7:06 PM, but clouds look likely through the evening, and tomorrow night clears up again. By the time the ship sails on November 1 it will be a half-lit last quarter moon, rising late that night over open water.
